title: One Elite High School’s Struggle Over Admissions

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于对设计的热爱以及围绕它的文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: You're just going to kind of put a number on me and that's going to determine my future.
sentences.zh: 你只是打算给我贴个标签，然后这就决定了我的未来。

sentences.en: I don't think it's serving every student as well as it needs to.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它能像预期的那样服务好每一位学生。

sentences.en: In recent months, we've seen a meaningful re-examination of this country's education system and the tests that often sit at the heart of admissions to the nation's top schools.
sentences.zh: 近几个月来，我们对这个国家的教育体系以及那些往往处于顶尖学校录取核心的考试进行了有意义的重新审视。

sentences.en: We have these very elite public schools that kids test into in this city.
sentences.zh: 在这个城市里，我们有一些孩子们通过考试才能进入的精英公立学校。

sentences.en: In the wake of George Floyd's murder, hard questions have been asked about who these admissions systems benefit.
sentences.zh: 在乔治·弗洛伊德被谋杀后，关于这些录取系统到底让谁受益，人们提出了尖锐的问题。

sentences.en: And last year, even though the public school system is made up 70% of Black and Hispanic children, only 10 Black students got into Stuyvesant.
sentences.zh: 去年，尽管公立学校系统中70%的学生是黑人和西班牙裔儿童，但只有10名黑人学生进入了史岱文森高中。

sentences.en: And who they leave out.
sentences.zh: 以及他们把谁排除在外。

sentences.en: The numbers, by and large, have not changed in recent years at the competitive high schools, which remain highly racially segregated, or I guess to be specific,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这些竞争激烈的公立高中的数据近年来并没有改变，它们依然保持着高度的种族隔离，或者我应该说得具体一点，

sentences.en: excluding Black and Latino students.
sentences.zh: 排斥了黑人和拉丁裔学生。

sentences.en: And after decades of resistance.
sentences.zh: 而且是在经历了数十年的抵制之后。

sentences.en: Well, the SAT has been a target of equity-minded reformers for a long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，长期以来，SAT考试一直是那些注重公平的改革者们的目标。

sentences.en: Real changes are being made.
sentences.zh: 真正的变革正在发生。

sentences.en: The SAT, the ACT standardized tests are out at UC.
sentences.zh: 加州大学已经取消了SAT和ACT标准化考试。

sentences.en: Harvard announced it will not require ACT or SAT scores for admission for the next four years.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学宣布，未来四年内将不再要求申请者提供ACT或SAT成绩。

sentences.en: And elite public high schools around the country that use so-called merit-based admission systeMs.
sentences.zh: 还有全国各地使用所谓“择优录取”系统的精英公立高中。

sentences.en: Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology has been rated the number one public high school in America.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·杰斐逊科技高中被评为全美第一的公立高中。

sentences.en: It has shifted its standards after accusations they were exclusionary to some minorities.
sentences.zh: 在被指责对某些少数族裔具有排他性后，它已经调整了标准。

sentences.en: Have finally begun to bend to pressure to replace those systeMs.
sentences.zh: 终于开始屈服于压力，着手更换这些系统。

sentences.en: Boston, this week, they also unanimously, their school committee, voted to change their entrance exam.
sentences.zh: 本周，波士顿学校委员会也一致投票决定更改他们的入学考试。

sentences.en: It was interesting because they talked about…
sentences.zh: 这很有意思，因为他们谈到了……

sentences.en: But amid the reforms, an uncomfortable reality has begun to emerge.
sentences.zh: 但在改革浪潮中，一个令人不安的现实开始浮现。

sentences.en: Parents of Asian American students are battling against the new standards in court.
sentences.zh: 亚裔学生的家长们正在法庭上对抗这些新标准。

sentences.en: That in trying to give better resources to Black students, many Asian Americans have come to feel that something is being taken away.
sentences.zh: 因为在试图为黑人学生提供更好资源的过程中，许多亚裔美国人开始感到自己被剥夺了某些东西。

sentences.en: And that in a conversation so often framed in terms of white and Black, they are being left out of the conversation altogether.
sentences.zh: 而且在这样一个通常以黑白视角构建的对话中，他们被完全排除在了讨论之外。

sentences.en: We are so diverse, but we were the wrong kind of diverse for the school board and the superintendent.
sentences.zh: 我们非常多元，但对于校董会和学监来说，我们是“错误的”多元。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues, Jay Caspian Kang and daily producer Jessica Chung, have the story of one high school in San Francisco where all these tensions have been playing out.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事杰伊·卡斯皮安·康和《每日新闻》制作人杰西卡·钟，将讲述旧金山一所高中发生的故事，所有的这些矛盾都在那里上演。

sentences.en: A high school that Jessica herself attended.
sentences.zh: 那也是杰西卡自己曾经就读过的高中。

sentences.en: It's Friday, June 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月24日，星期五。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 挺好的。

sentences.en: Just bringing back memories.
sentences.zh: 只是勾起了一些回忆。

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有一点。

sentences.en: Everything looks the same.
sentences.zh: 一切看起来都没变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: When were you here?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候在这里上学的？

sentences.en: So earlier this year on a foggy San Francisco morning, Jess and I arranged to meet up on the street outside of Lowell.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，在一个雾蒙蒙的旧金山早晨，杰西和我约定在洛威尔高中外面的街道上见面。

sentences.en: How's it feel to be at Lowell High School?
sentences.zh: 回到洛威尔高中感觉如何？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I've thought about this school a lot, you know, over the past few years just because of what I generally write about and what this school means within this community.
sentences.zh: 过去几年我经常想到这所学校，你知道，因为我通常写的内容，以及这所学校在这个社区中的意义。

sentences.en: You know, I live here in the Bay Area and it is a little bit surreal to actually be here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我就住在湾区，能真正站在这里感觉有点超现实。

sentences.en: The first thing you need to understand about Lowell, to understand why we sound like this standing outside of a high school, is that it's not just any high school.
sentences.zh: 要理解为什么我们站在一所高中外面录音，你首先需要了解洛威尔，它可不是什么普通的公立高中。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I guess we'll put on our masks to go inside.
sentences.zh: 那我想我们得戴上口罩进去了。

sentences.en: Lowell is kind of a famous school.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔是一所很有名的学校。

sentences.en: One of the highest performing public schools in the state of California.
sentences.zh: 它是加州表现最好的公立学校之一。

sentences.en: America's best high school is 2016, 2019.
sentences.zh: 2016年、2019年全美最佳高中。

sentences.en: And frequently ranked among the best public schools in the country.
sentences.zh: 并且经常被评为全国最好的公立学校之一。

sentences.en: Is this it?
sentences.zh: 是这里吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is it.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这儿。

sentences.en: A Lowell tradition.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔的传统。

sentences.en: And there's a number of distinguished people who have graduated from Lowell.
sentences.zh: 有很多杰出人士都是从洛威尔毕业的。

sentences.en: Okay, let's check this out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来看看。

sentences.en: Yeah, Stephen Breyer.
sentences.zh: 没错，斯蒂芬·布雷耶。

sentences.en: Is he the most distinguished alumni that people talk about?
sentences.zh: 他是人们谈论的最杰出的校友吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Let's see here.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: Oh, and Alexander Calder.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有亚历山大·考尔德。

sentences.en: Alexander Calder.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·考尔德。

sentences.en: 1916 kinetic artiSt.
sentences.zh: 1916届，动态雕塑艺术家。

sentences.en: Yeah, the mobile guy.
sentences.zh: 对，就是做动态雕塑的那位。

sentences.en: I wonder what level of success you'd have to cross to end up here.
sentences.zh: 我在想，得达到什么程度的成功才能被挂在这里。

sentences.en: You should petition.
sentences.zh: 你应该去申请一下。

sentences.en: You should be a producer of the hit podcast, The Daily.
sentences.zh: 你应该成为热门播客《每日新闻》的制作人。

sentences.en: This board would have to get way big to accommodate that.
sentences.zh: 那这块板子得做得大得多才能容纳下那个成就。

sentences.en: So a lot of big names have come out of Lowell.
sentences.zh: 所以，很多大人物都是从洛威尔走出来的。

sentences.en: But if you live outside of San Francisco and you've heard about the school, it's probably because of its admission system.
sentences.zh: 但如果你住在旧金山以外，并且听说过这所学校，那很可能是因为它的录取制度。

sentences.en: Students are admitted based on grades and test scores.
sentences.zh: 学生是根据成绩和考试分数录取的。

sentences.en: And just like other merit-based public schools in places like Virginia and New York City, there's been a lot of controversy here over who gets in and who doesn't.
sentences.zh: 就像弗吉尼亚州和纽约市等地的其他择优录取公立学校一样，这里关于谁能入学、谁不能入学的争议一直很多。

sentences.en: I will say, walking around.
sentences.zh: 我得说，走在校园里。

sentences.en: This is a very Asian school.
sentences.zh: 这是一所非常“亚裔”的学校。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: There's like a ton of Asian kids.
sentences.zh: 这里有大量的亚裔孩子。

sentences.en: There's just so many.
sentences.zh: 真的太多了。

sentences.en: What percentage would you say Asian it looks like just walking around?
sentences.zh: 你觉得走在校园里，亚裔学生的比例大概是多少？

sentences.en: Right now, it feels like 90.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉有90%。

sentences.en: I know that's not the actual number, but it just feels that way, right?
sentences.zh: 我知道这不是实际数字，但感觉就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And like, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的。

sentences.en: Lowell plays a very specific role in the San Francisco school system.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔在旧金山学校系统中扮演着非常特殊的角色。

sentences.en: A lot of white, upper-middle-class families send their kids to the city's private schools.
sentences.zh: 许多白人中上层家庭把孩子送到市里的私立学校。

sentences.en: So while Lowell might have a kind of elite status in the city.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然洛威尔在城里可能有一种精英地位。

sentences.en: I can't get over how many signs there are about how good the school is.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法相信这里有这么多关于学校有多优秀的标语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's only within the context of the types of kids in San Francisco who actually go to public school.
sentences.zh: 那只是在旧金山那些真正上公立学校的孩子们的范围内而言。

sentences.en: That's mostly working class and middle-class kids of color.
sentences.zh: 那主要是工薪阶层和中产阶级的有色人种孩子。

sentences.en: You know, despite all that, it doesn't feel like one of these storied places that you go to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尽管如此，它感觉并不像那种你所向往的传奇名校。

sentences.en: This is still like a very much like a city public school, you know, that just has a few more banners than normal ones.
sentences.zh: 这依然非常像一所普通的城市公立学校，你知道，只是比普通的学校多了几条横幅而已。

sentences.en: It just doesn't feel that different.
sentences.zh: 它感觉并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel exclusive in a way.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上并不让人觉得排外。

sentences.en: It feels actually, you know, just like a public school.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它感觉就像一所普通的公立学校。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The reality, obviously, is somewhat different.
sentences.zh: 显然，现实情况有些不同。

sentences.en: And so, because of that status, Lowell has become a school that represents something very important to a lot of families in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于这种地位，洛威尔已经成为一所对旧金山许多家庭来说意义重大的学校。

sentences.en: It's thought of as this supercharger of class mobility.
sentences.zh: 它被认为是阶级流动的“增压器”。

sentences.en: So, if a kid works hard and gets admitted, it's recognition that the country is rewarding that work, regardless of where they come from.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个孩子努力学习并被录取，这被视为国家对这种努力的认可，无论他们来自哪里。

sentences.en: But that admission system has resulted in a student body that looks very different from the rest of the district.
sentences.zh: 但这种录取制度导致学生群体看起来与该学区的其他地方截然不同。

sentences.en: Last year, for example, 57% of students at Lowell were Asian, compared to 34% in the district.
sentences.zh: 例如，去年洛威尔的学生中有57%是亚裔，而整个学区的比例为34%。

sentences.en: And when it comes to Latino and Black students, it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 而对于拉丁裔和黑人学生来说，情况则恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Last year, less than 2% of students at Lowell identified as Black, even though 6% of the district did.
sentences.zh: 去年，洛威尔只有不到2%的学生是黑人，尽管该学区黑人学生的比例为6%。

sentences.en: And critics say that's created a discriminatory, hostile environment for Black students in particular.
sentences.zh: 批评人士称，这为黑人学生创造了一种歧视性的、充满敌意的环境。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hey, are you Aubrey?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你是奥布里吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Good, I guess.
sentences.zh: 还行吧。

sentences.en: Good, yeah.
sentences.zh: 挺好的，是啊。

sentences.en: We met up with Aubrey Chicory and a friend of hers at the front of the school during a lunch break.
sentences.zh: 我们在午休时间在学校门口见到了奥布里·奇科里和她的朋友。

sentences.en: Aubrey is a junior at Lowell, and this year, she was one of just 44 Black students at the school, in a student body of more than 2,700.
sentences.zh: 奥布里是洛威尔的一名高二学生，今年，在超过2700名学生中，她是仅有的44名黑人学生之一。

sentences.en: I have a question.
sentences.zh: 我有个问题。

sentences.en: You know, like, just from being here the last two days, it's just my observation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，仅仅是这两天待在这里，这是我的观察。

sentences.en: It seems like socially things are very segregated in a way that's actually kind of surprising to me, because I grew up in North Carolina and it wasn't like this.
sentences.zh: 社交方面似乎非常隔离，这让我感到有点惊讶，因为我在北卡罗来纳州长大，情况并不是这样。

sentences.en: Can you just tell, like, what's the social life like here in terms of race to kids?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我，这里的孩子们在种族方面的社交生活是什么样的吗？

sentences.en: Is it pretty segregated?
sentences.zh: 是不是相当隔离？

sentences.en: I mean, I know, like, the Black and Brown kids, we hang with each other more because we are the minority at this school.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道，黑人和棕色人种的孩子，我们更多地待在一起，因为我们是这所学校的少数群体。

sentences.en: But I get, like, if there were a lot more Black and Brown students at this school, you would see more diverse groups of people.
sentences.zh: 但我明白，如果这所学校有更多的黑人和棕色人种学生，你会看到更多元化的群体。

sentences.en: Aubrey's parents wanted her to go to Lowell because a cousin had gone there, and they saw the opportunities the school provided.
sentences.zh: 奥布里的父母希望她去洛威尔，因为她的表亲曾在那儿上学，他们看到了学校提供的机会。

sentences.en: So Aubrey applied and got in.
sentences.zh: 于是奥布里申请并被录取了。

sentences.en: What did your cousin tell you about Lowell?
sentences.zh: 你的表亲跟你说了关于洛威尔的什么？

sentences.en: She said it was very intense and that a lot of things would happen, like, regarding racism.
sentences.zh: 她说这里竞争非常激烈，而且会发生很多关于种族主义的事情。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I was very much nervous because I didn't see a lot of kids who looked like me.
sentences.zh: 而且，我是真的很紧张，因为我没看到多少长得像我一样的孩子。

sentences.en: I was often the only Black kid in my class.
sentences.zh: 我经常是班里唯一的黑人孩子。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: You mentioned to me over the phone an incident that happened, I think, freshman year.
sentences.zh: 你在电话里跟我提到过一件发生在你高一时候的事情。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about that, what happened there?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我那件事吗，当时发生了什么？

sentences.en: So I had a friend in freshman year, ex-friend now.
sentences.zh: 我高一的时候有个朋友，现在已经不是了。

sentences.en: He would use the N-word around me and joke about African Americans.
sentences.zh: 他会在我面前用“黑鬼”（N-word）这个词，还会拿非裔美国人开玩笑。

sentences.en: And one day he posted a story of how to ask a Black girl out to prom with a picture of someone holding a bouquet of cotton.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他发了一个动态，内容是如何邀请一个黑人女孩去参加毕业舞会，配图是一个人拿着一束棉花。

sentences.en: And I didn't know how to report that to admin at that moment, so I, like, held it on.
sentences.zh: 当时我不知道该怎么向校方举报，所以我只能忍着。

sentences.en: Like, I had to keep it to myself for days.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把这件事藏在心里好几天。

sentences.en: And I, like, didn't know who to tell until the Padlet incident.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该告诉谁，直到发生了“Padlet事件”。

sentences.en: The Padlet incident is a term you hear a lot when you talk to students at Lowell.
sentences.zh: “Padlet事件”是你和洛威尔的学生交谈时经常听到的一个词。

sentences.en: And this is the thing that happened last year that Jaya told me helps explain the whole school board recall.
sentences.zh: 这就是去年发生的事情，贾亚告诉我，这有助于解释整个校董会罢免事件。

sentences.en: And it happened against this backdrop at Lowell.
sentences.zh: 而且它发生在洛威尔的这种背景之下。

sentences.en: A controversial admissions system and a widespread feeling among Black students that being Black at Lowell was not a comfortable experience.
sentences.zh: 一个充满争议的录取制度，以及黑人学生中普遍存在的一种感觉：在洛威尔做黑人并不是一种舒适的体验。

sentences.en: Everyone on campus can tell their own version of the Padlet story.
sentences.zh: 校园里的每个人都能讲出他们自己版本的Padlet故事。

sentences.en: Uh, we've been talking to students, and one thing that keeps coming up is this thing called the Padlet incident.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们一直在和学生们交谈，有一件事不断被提及，就是这个所谓的“Padlet事件”。

sentences.en: I was wondering if you could, from your perspective, tell me how you found out about that incident.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能从你的角度告诉我，你是怎么发现那件事的？

sentences.en: Where were you when you found out?
sentences.zh: 你发现的时候在哪里？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it was, I think it was in, I think it was in February.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是在二月份。

sentences.en: It was late January, 2021, heading into February, and Black History Month.
sentences.zh: 那是2021年1月底，快到二月的时候，也是黑人历史月。

sentences.en: It was just an average day.
sentences.zh: 那只是平常的一天。

sentences.en: It was, like, Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 大概是周三。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure this was over distance learning.
sentences.zh: 我很确定当时是在远程学习期间。

sentences.en: This was during distance learning.
sentences.zh: 那是在远程教学期间。

sentences.en: That morning, students logged on to their homeroom classes to attend an anti-racism lesson.
sentences.zh: 那天早上，学生们登录各自的班级参加一堂反种族主义课程。

sentences.en: And as part of this lesson, students clicked on a link that took them to an online brainstorming board called Padlet.
sentences.zh: 作为课程的一部分，学生们点击了一个链接，跳转到一个名为 Padlet 的在线头脑风暴板。

sentences.en: There is this thing called Padlet where you could post anonymous messages to answer, like, questions of, like, how do you be less racist?
sentences.zh: Padlet 这个东西可以让你发布匿名信息来回答问题，比如：如何减少种族歧视？

sentences.en: How can students be anti-racist at Lowell?
sentences.zh: 学生们在洛威尔高中如何做到反种族歧视？

sentences.en: On this particular day, students were being asked to engage with the question of how the phrase, all lives matter, could be hurtful and undermine Black lives matter.
sentences.zh: 在这一天，学生们被要求探讨“‘所有生命都很重要’（All Lives Matter）这一短语为何会造成伤害并削弱‘黑人的命也是命’（Black Lives Matter）”这一问题。

sentences.en: But when students opened up the Padlet board…
sentences.zh: 但当学生们打开 Padlet 看板时……

sentences.en: At that point, I saw just very graphic images, inappropriate slurs, very racist, like, sentiments.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，我看到的尽是些非常露骨的图片、不当的辱骂词汇，还有非常种族主义的言论。

sentences.en: It had essentially been vandalized and was just covered in racist, hateful images.
sentences.zh: 它基本上被破坏了，到处都是种族主义和仇恨的图片。

sentences.en: One post was an image of a Black man giving himself oral sex with the caption, Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 其中一条帖子是一张黑人男性进行口交的图片，配文是“黑人的命也是命”。

sentences.en: I was horrified.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, I thought I was on some wrong website.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我以为自己进错了网站。

sentences.en: I thought, like, no way this is happening on a school-sanctioned activity.
sentences.zh: 我想，这怎么可能发生在学校批准的活动中呢？

sentences.en: And within a few hours, images from the message board circulate around the whole school.
sentences.zh: 几小时内，留言板上的图片就在全校传开了。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, you see on Instagram, like, everyone's like, oh, this is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 突然间，你在 Instagram 上看到每个人都在说，这太不可接受了。

sentences.en: Very quickly, the school administration announced that the board had been hacked and that it was investigating the matter.
sentences.zh: 学校管理层很快宣布看板被黑了，并表示正在调查此事。

sentences.en: And if it turned out to have been a student, they would take disciplinary action.
sentences.zh: 如果查出是学生所为，他们将采取纪律处分。

sentences.en: You know, the administration didn't really react to it in the most effective way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，管理层对此事的反应并不是最有效的。

sentences.en: Oh, we got this under control, guys.
sentences.zh: 噢，伙计们，我们已经控制住局面了。

sentences.en: But many students said they thought the response was inadequate.
sentences.zh: 但许多学生表示，他们认为这种回应是不够的。

sentences.en: That in talking about the board being hacked, maybe by a student, maybe by an outsider, the school was characterizing it as a kind of cybersecurity issue
sentences.zh: 学校谈论看板被黑，可能是学生所为，也可能是外人所为，这实际上是将问题定性为一种网络安全问题，

sentences.en: rather than as a larger issue of racism within the school.
sentences.zh: 而不是将其视为学校内部更广泛的种族主义问题。

sentences.en: I would define that as the moment where things really were set in motion.
sentences.zh: 我认为那一刻就是事情真正开始发酵的起点。

sentences.en: A few days later, on January 26th...
sentences.zh: 几天后，即 1 月 26 日……

sentences.en: January 26th is now called to order.
sentences.zh: 现在宣布 1 月 26 日会议开始。

sentences.en: Roll call, please.
sentences.zh: 请点名。

sentences.en: The school board for the San Francisco Unified School District, SFUSD, met virtually for the first time census incident.
sentences.zh: 旧金山联合学区（SFUSD）的校董会自事件发生后首次以线上形式召开了会议。

sentences.en: Students can speak to any item on the agenda.
sentences.zh: 学生可以就议程上的任何事项发言。

sentences.en: So please raise your hand if you care to speak right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你现在想发言，请举手。

sentences.en: And during the meeting...
sentences.zh: 在会议期间……

sentences.en: Hi, can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 嗨，能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: We can, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 可以，请讲。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Micah.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫 Micah。

sentences.en: I'm a Lowell sophomore, and I want to talk about the Lowell Padlet incident.
sentences.zh: 我是洛威尔高中的二年级学生，我想谈谈洛威尔的 Padlet 事件。

sentences.en: A number of students from Lowell called in.
sentences.zh: 许多洛威尔的学生打进电话发言。

sentences.en: Hello, my name is Aaliyah Hunter.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫 Aaliyah Hunter。

sentences.en: I am a sophomore and BSU treasurer at Lowell High School.
sentences.zh: 我是洛威尔高中的二年级学生，也是黑人学生联盟（BSU）的财务主管。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Nancy Garcia from Lowell High School.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是来自洛威尔高中的 Nancy Garcia。

sentences.en: I'm a senior.
sentences.zh: 我是四年级学生。

sentences.en: And what started to pour out were stories, like Aubrey's, of what it felt like to be among the small number of Black and Brown students at Lowell.
sentences.zh: 随后涌现出的，是像 Aubrey 那样的故事，讲述了作为洛威尔少数黑人和棕色人种学生之一的感受。

sentences.en: We really need to see something from administration.
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要看到管理层有所作为。

sentences.en: We really need to see something done about the racist acts that have gone on for years and years on end.
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要看到针对多年来持续不断的种族主义行为采取行动。

sentences.en: And then, alumni and parents start to weigh in.
sentences.zh: 接着，校友和家长们也开始发表意见。

sentences.en: Hello, caller, are you there?
sentences.zh: 你好，通话者，你在吗？

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Sarah Brandt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫 Sarah Brandt。

sentences.en: I really appreciate so much the emotional and physical labor of Black students and families and adults sharing out today.
sentences.zh: 我非常感谢今天分享经历的黑人学生、家庭和成年人们所付出的情感和体力劳动。

sentences.en: I went to Lowell.
sentences.zh: 我曾就读于洛威尔高中。

sentences.en: It has not changed.
sentences.zh: 它一点都没变。

sentences.en: Lowell's culture, on so many levels, continues to amplify anti-Black racism.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔的文化在许多层面上都在持续助长反黑人种族主义。

sentences.en: So I just want to add that as an SFUSD teacher, I continue to ask why Lowell as an institution is allowed to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名旧金山联合学区的老师，我还要问，为什么洛威尔作为一个机构还能被允许存在？

sentences.en: And what you heard was years of built-up frustration.
sentences.zh: 你所听到的是多年来积压的挫败感。

sentences.en: We should not have to keep coming back, time after time after time, with this same issue.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该一次又一次地为了同样的问题回来抗争。

sentences.en: How long is Lowell going to be allowed to be this racist powerhouse?
sentences.zh: 洛威尔还要被允许做这种种族主义的堡垒多久？

sentences.en: And SFUSD is escalating.
sentences.zh: 而旧金山联合学区正在升级事态。

sentences.en: I apologize, but we have to make a change.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，但我们必须做出改变。

sentences.en: I just hope and I pray that by the time my three-month-old is ready to go to high school, that Lowell will be changed.
sentences.zh: 我只是希望并祈祷，等到我三个月大的孩子上高中时，洛威尔已经改变了。

sentences.en: Do we have to wait that long?
sentences.zh: 我们非要等那么久吗？

sentences.en: When are we going to demand change?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能要求改变？

sentences.en: When are we going to make it happen?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候才能让它实现？

sentences.en: Ask yourself, how long does it have to happen?
sentences.zh: 问问你自己，这种情况还要持续多久？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: This goes on for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: And throughout the meeting, a student delegate on the board and president of Lowell's Black Student Union, Siobhan Hines-Foster, speaks up repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 在整个会议期间，校董会学生代表兼洛威尔黑人学生联盟主席 Siobhan Hines-Foster 多次发言。

sentences.en: How much longer?
sentences.zh: 还要多久？

sentences.en: I mean, it's truly a question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的是个问题。

sentences.en: How much longer?
sentences.zh: 还要多久？

sentences.en: And she's among the strongest voices that day, calling on the school board to do something about what they're hearing.
sentences.zh: 她是那天最有力的声音之一，呼吁校董会对他们所听到的情况采取行动。

sentences.en: Y'all sit up here with your SFUSD-centered, student-centered posters, anti-racist lessons that are hella janky, and just let this school do whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 你们坐在上面，挂着以学区为中心、以学生为中心的标语，搞着那些烂透了的反种族主义课程，却任由这所学校为所欲为。

sentences.en: You need to fix it.
sentences.zh: 你们必须解决它。

sentences.en: Why do I have to go to school to be traumatized to get my credits to graduate?
sentences.zh: 为什么我上学为了拿学分毕业，却要遭受创伤？

sentences.en: It's not just me.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是我。

sentences.en: Alumni.
sentences.zh: 校友们。

sentences.en: Alumni before alumni.
sentences.zh: 一代又一代的校友。

sentences.en: It's ghetto.
sentences.zh: 这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's raggedy.
sentences.zh: 这太破烂了。

sentences.en: And it's your fault.
sentences.zh: 而且这是你们的错。

sentences.en: And what you hear in response from the largely Black and Latino school board members.
sentences.zh: 而你听到的是以黑人和拉丁裔为主的校董会成员的回应。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: And I really want to emphasize that there is so much burden our students are taking on that they've been sharing this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我真的想强调，我们的学生承担了太多的负担，他们一直在反复分享这些经历。

sentences.en: Is a number of board members really affirming the people coming forward that day.
sentences.zh: 许多校董会成员确实在肯定那天站出来的人们。

sentences.en: I'm not surprised.
sentences.zh: 我并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And at some point, the board's vice president, Allison Collins, who is Black and had criticized Lowell for race issues in the past,
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，校董会副主席 Allison Collins（她是黑人，过去曾批评过洛威尔的种族问题）

sentences.en: connects these accounts of pervasive racism that they're hearing to the school's admissions policy and the efforts by the city to protect it.
sentences.zh: 将他们听到的这些普遍存在的种族主义叙述，与学校的招生政策以及城市保护该政策的努力联系了起来。

sentences.en: Racism is political officials speaking up on behalf of a selective enrollment system that perpetuates segregation.
sentences.zh: 种族主义就是政治官员为维持种族隔离的选择性招生制度辩护。

sentences.en: A number of board members jump on that, including Matt Sanchez.
sentences.zh: 包括 Matt Sanchez 在内的多名校董会成员对此表示赞同。

sentences.en: Um, Lowell has been a festering pool of racism for so long.
sentences.zh: 嗯，洛威尔长期以来一直是种族主义的温床。

sentences.en: It's been one of the main reasons why I've wanted a change for so long in the admissions policy.
sentences.zh: 这也是我长期以来一直希望改变招生政策的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: Who explicitly calls for a change.
sentences.zh: 他明确呼吁进行改革。

sentences.en: And it has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这必须停止。

sentences.en: We have to commit ourselves, colleagues.
sentences.zh: 同事们，我们必须做出承诺。

sentences.en: We have to commit ourselves to ending the admissions process.
sentences.zh: 我们必须承诺结束这种招生程序。

sentences.en: We have to make that verbal commitment.
sentences.zh: 我们必须做出口头承诺。

sentences.en: And he's saying, this has to end now.
sentences.zh: 他在说，这一切必须现在结束。

sentences.en: And then we have to do it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们必须付诸行动。

sentences.en: And just over a week later, the BSU, led by Siobhan, releases a list of 23 demands.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一周多后，由 Siobhan 领导的黑人学生联盟发布了一份包含 23 项要求的清单。

sentences.en: And number one on that list is to change the admissions policy at Lowell from a merit-based system to a lottery-based one.
sentences.zh: 清单上的第一条就是将洛威尔的招生政策从择优录取制改为抽签制。

sentences.en: The system used by the other public schools in the district in admitting their students.
sentences.zh: 这是该学区其他公立学校录取学生时所采用的制度。

sentences.en: One, resolution number 212-2A1 in response to ongoing systemic racism at Lowell High School.
sentences.zh: 第一，关于应对洛威尔高中持续存在的系统性种族主义的第 212-2A1 号决议。

sentences.en: And on February 9th, 2021, just three weeks after the Padlet incident at Lowell High School, the school board reconvened to consider a resolution.
sentences.zh: 2021 年 2 月 9 日，在洛威尔高中 Padlet 事件发生仅三周后，校董会重新召集会议审议一项决议。

sentences.en: Commissioners Allison M.
sentences.zh: 委员 Allison M.

sentences.en: Collins, Gabriela Lopez, Matt Alexander, and student delegates Siobhan Hine Foster and Katia Correa Almanza.
sentences.zh: Collins、Gabriela Lopez、Matt Alexander 以及学生代表 Siobhan Hine Foster 和 Katia Correa Almanza。

sentences.en: Allison Collins and two other school board members joined Siobhan and another student in introducing a proposal that would eliminate Lowell's merit-based admission system.
sentences.zh: Allison Collins 和另外两名校董会成员与 Siobhan 及另一名学生共同提出了一项提案，旨在取消洛威尔的择优录取制度。

sentences.en: Perpetuates the culture of white supremacy and racial abuse towards Black and Latinx students.
sentences.zh: 这助长了白人至上主义和针对黑人及拉丁裔学生的种族虐待文化。

sentences.en: What followed was another hours-long meeting, this one 10 hours, and toward the end of the night.
sentences.zh: 随后又是一场长达数小时的会议，这次持续了 10 个小时，在深夜临近结束时。

sentences.en: And we will move to roll call vote.
sentences.zh: 现在进行点名表决。

sentences.en: The board called its vote.
sentences.zh: 校董会进行了投票。

sentences.en: Roll call, Ms. Cosco.
sentences.zh: 点名，Cosco 女士。

sentences.en: Thank you, Commissioner.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，委员。

sentences.en: Mr. Alexander?
sentences.zh: Alexander 先生？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Mr. Bogus?
sentences.zh: Bogus 先生？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 反对。

sentences.en: Ms. Collins?
sentences.zh: Collins 女士？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Ms. Lamb?
sentences.zh: Lamb 女士？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 反对。

sentences.en: Mr. Maliga?
sentences.zh: Maliga 先生？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Mr. Sanchez?
sentences.zh: Sanchez 先生？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Ms. Lopez?
sentences.zh: Lopez 女士？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Of the seven board members...
sentences.zh: 在七名校董会成员中……

sentences.en: That's five eyes.
sentences.zh: 那是五票赞成。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: ...five voted in favor of the resolution.
sentences.zh: ……五人投票支持该决议。

sentences.en: The two other members, including the only Asian member of the board, voted against it.
sentences.zh: 另外两名成员，包括校董会中唯一的亚裔成员，投了反对票。

sentences.en: And after decades of controversy and debate...
sentences.zh: 经过几十年的争议和辩论……

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, everyone, for tonight's discussion.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家今晚的讨论。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: That'll work for the edge.
sentences.zh: 这对于边缘群体来说是有效的。

sentences.en: Yes, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Lowell's merit-based admission system was eliminated with a 5-2 vote.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔的择优录取制度以 5 比 2 的投票结果被废除。

sentences.en: Meaning that overnight, the city's premier public school would function like every other school in the city.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一夜之间，这所城市首屈一指的公立学校将像城里其他所有学校一样运作。

sentences.en: The next year's freshman class would not be considered based on their grades and test scores, but rather through a lottery system, where any student who applied would have equal
sentences.zh: 明年入学的新生将不再根据成绩和考试分数来考虑，而是通过抽签系统，任何申请的学生都将有平等的机会

sentences.en: chance of being randomly selected for admission.
sentences.zh: 被随机选中入学。

sentences.en: And so, a year after the school board meeting, with Lowell's merit-based admission system now done away with, we wanted to talk to students at the school about where things stood.
sentences.zh: 因此，在校董会会议一年后，随着洛威尔的择优录取制度被废除，我们想和学校的学生谈谈现状如何。

sentences.en: And from what we'd heard, that all depended on who you talked to.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这完全取决于你和谁谈。

sentences.en: Yeah, stereotyping us like...
sentences.zh: 是啊，给我们贴标签，就像……

sentences.en: Aubrey, the student whose cousin had warned her about coming to Lowell, says that she had been part of the push to change the system.
sentences.zh: Aubrey，那位曾被表亲警告不要来洛威尔的学生，说她曾参与推动改变这一制度。

sentences.en: She thought it would help.
sentences.zh: 她认为这会有所帮助。

sentences.en: My experiences going, walking down through the halls, feeling like an imposter, like having imposter syndrome at this school, I feel like merit system really fueled that.
sentences.zh: 我在走廊里走动时的经历，感觉自己像个冒名顶替者，在这所学校有冒名顶替综合症，我觉得择优录取制度确实加剧了这一点。

sentences.en: And in terms of how the school looks, it has made a difference.
sentences.zh: 就学校的面貌而言，它确实带来了改变。

sentences.en: This year's freshman class was the first to be admitted through the lottery process.
sentences.zh: 今年的新生班级是第一批通过抽签程序录取的。

sentences.en: The percentage of Black students in the freshman class doubled to 4%.
sentences.zh: 新生中黑人学生的比例翻了一番，达到 4%。

sentences.en: Latino students rose from 13% to 21%.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔学生的比例从 13% 上升到 21%。

sentences.en: And those increases meant that the percentage of White and Asian students fell.
sentences.zh: 而这些增长意味着白人和亚裔学生的比例下降了。

sentences.en: And how do you personally feel a year in a lottery system?

sentences.zh: 是有什么会议吗？

sentences.en: His name is Ben Chen, and like Aubrey, he's a junior at Lowell.
sentences.zh: 他叫本·陈，和奥布里一样，是洛威尔高中的大三学生。

sentences.en: Did you just get home from school?
sentences.zh: 你刚从学校回来吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he greets us near the front of the building we'd been admiring on the corner.
sentences.zh: 他在我们刚才一直赞叹的拐角处那栋楼前迎接我们。

sentences.en: What's the deal with this building?
sentences.zh: 这栋楼是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It's a new building that was recently built in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋最近在旧金山新建的楼房。

sentences.en: So my family won the lottery for this, and so we've been living here since.
sentences.zh: 我们家抽中了这里的住房名额，所以从那以后我们就一直住在这里。

sentences.en: Is it a different type of place from where you're used to living?
sentences.zh: 这和你以前住的地方感觉不一样吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: It's much better.
sentences.zh: 好多了。

sentences.en: The old place I used to live in, it was like really bad.
sentences.zh: 我以前住的那个老地方，真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: There was like ants and rats all over, and it's like the whole building was infested with them.
sentences.zh: 到处都是蚂蚁和老鼠，整栋楼都被它们侵占了。

sentences.en: So it was a really horrible, horrible place to spend the first 13 years of your life.
sentences.zh: 所以，在你人生最初的13年里，那真是一个非常、非常糟糕的居住环境。

sentences.en: But for Ben's family, it represented progress.
sentences.zh: 但对本（Ben）的家庭来说，这代表着进步。

sentences.en: They immigrated here from China in 2007, when Ben was two, and started to build a new life here.
sentences.zh: 他们于2007年从中国移民到这里，当时本才两岁，他们开始在这里建立新的生活。

sentences.en: During those early days, none of us spoke English, so they like really had trouble to really find a job.
sentences.zh: 在那些早期的日子里，我们都不会说英语，所以他们找工作真的遇到了很大的困难。

sentences.en: And I remember my parents going to community college classes to get to know some basic English.
sentences.zh: 我记得我父母去社区大学上课，为了学习一些基础的英语。

sentences.en: As he got older, Ben became the only one in the family who spoke fluent English,
sentences.zh: 随着年龄增长，本成了家里唯一能说流利英语的人，

sentences.en: and he would often translate for his parents, helping them pay bills, navigate government services, food banks, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 他经常为父母当翻译，帮他们付账单、办理政府业务、去食物银行，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: You know, let's just go into like some of the schooling part of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们来聊聊关于上学的部分吧。

sentences.en: You know, like when did you first start thinking about going to Lowell?
sentences.zh: 你是从什么时候开始考虑去洛威尔（Lowell）高中的？

sentences.en: You know, like how old were you, and like how did you start preparing?
sentences.zh: 你当时多大？又是怎么开始准备的？

sentences.en: Well, so I first heard about Lowell in a fifth grade PTA meeting between my fifth grade teachers and my parents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我第一次听说洛威尔是在五年级的一次家长会（PTA）上，是我五年级的老师和我父母提到的。

sentences.en: And, you know, my parents at the time, I don't believe that they knew what Lowell High School was either.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当时我父母也不太了解洛威尔高中是什么学校。

sentences.en: Ben says his dad was skeptical about the long commute across the city.
sentences.zh: 本说他父亲对跨越整个城市去上学持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: He believed that my mother really wanted me to go.
sentences.zh: 他认为是我母亲真的很想让我去。

sentences.en: But for his mom, the school represented the path to a better life, the reason they'd come here.
sentences.zh: 但对他母亲来说，这所学校代表着通往更好生活的道路，也是他们来到这里的原因。

sentences.en: I'm going to bear down on this idea that it can provide you with a better life, right?
sentences.zh: 我要强调一个观点，那就是它能为你提供更好的生活，对吧？

sentences.en: Or with some form of like even class mobility, right?
sentences.zh: 或者说提供某种形式的阶层流动，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you're a working class kid here in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 因为你是在旧金山的一个工薪阶层孩子。

sentences.en: How does it lead to a better life?
sentences.zh: 它怎么就能带来更好的生活呢？

sentences.en: You know, let's say that I didn't get to Lowell and I went to a less academically inclined school.
sentences.zh: 假设我没能进入洛威尔，而是去了一所学术氛围没那么浓厚的学校。

sentences.en: Um, I do feel like I would be less motivated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我的动力会减少。

sentences.en: Um, even though like I'm not being pressured by my parents to get into a good college, I feel pressure from my peers to get into a good college.
sentences.zh: 嗯，即使我父母没有给我压力让我考上好大学，但我从同龄人那里感受到了考好大学的压力。

sentences.en: And seeing the amount of emphasis that they have on getting into a good college, I guess I also do feel some of that pressure.
sentences.zh: 看到他们对考上好大学的重视程度，我想我也确实感受到了那种压力。

sentences.en: So, I absolutely see that Lowell did offer me a better high school life than if I went to another high school.
sentences.zh: 所以，我绝对认为洛威尔确实为我提供了比去其他高中更好的高中生活。

sentences.en: Um, you know, like one thing I wanted to ask you is that like you have members of the San Francisco school board, but also like some activist people, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，有一件事我想问你，就是你有旧金山教育委员会的成员，还有一些活动人士，嗯，

sentences.en: not just here in San Francisco, but around the country.
sentences.zh: 不仅是在旧金山，在全国各地也是如此。

sentences.en: And like when they talk about places like Lowell, they basically say that the Asian kids at these schools are rich and that they're white adjacent, you know,
sentences.zh: 当他们谈论像洛威尔这样的学校时，他们基本上说这些学校里的亚裔孩子都很富有，而且他们是“白人附庸”，你知道，

sentences.en: like how does that make you feel?
sentences.zh: 这让你感觉如何？

sentences.en: It makes me feel completely ignored.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到完全被忽视了。

sentences.en: Um, you know, from my, from what I say, Lowell, a lot of the Asian kids like me, they aren't rich, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，就我所见，洛威尔很多像我一样的亚裔孩子，他们并不富有，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, they're also just poor immigrant kids like me and we feel ignored, right?
sentences.zh: 他们也只是像我一样的贫困移民孩子，我们感到被忽视了，对吧？

sentences.en: We feel ignored that these politicians and the media, they're like overlooking the Asians that did come to this country with nothing but their clothes.
sentences.zh: 我们感到被忽视了，因为这些政客和媒体，他们忽略了那些来到这个国家时除了身上穿的衣服外一无所有的亚裔。

sentences.en: It makes me feel really angry, right?
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常愤怒，对吧？

sentences.en: When people say that Asians are enabling white supremacy because I absolutely do not see that as a case.
sentences.zh: 当人们说亚裔在助长白人至上主义时，我绝对不认为事实是这样的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, I remember in a military school and middle school, you know, people did tell me to go back to my own country.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我记得在军事学校和中学时，人们确实叫我滚回自己的国家去。

sentences.en: Uh, people did, you know, call me slurs and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 人们确实，你知道，用侮辱性的词汇称呼我之类的。

sentences.en: And that experience of racism and being also called an enabler of white supremacists, that just makes us feel livid, right?
sentences.zh: 那种经历过种族歧视，却又被指责为白人至上主义的帮凶，这只会让我们感到愤怒，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we are the victims of white supremacy and they're saying that we somehow enable it.
sentences.zh: 因为我们才是白人至上主义的受害者，而他们却说我们以某种方式助长了它。

sentences.en: I just want to clarify something, which is that, um, it sounds like one of the politicians you're referring to is Alison Carter.
sentences.zh: 我只想澄清一件事，那就是，嗯，听起来你提到的其中一位政客是艾莉森·卡特（Alison Carter）。

sentences.en: A board member who accused Asians of using white supremacy to get ahead.
sentences.zh: 一位指责亚裔利用白人至上主义来获得优势的教委成员。

sentences.en: And that was also written in the resolution to change Lowell's emission system.
sentences.zh: 这也写在了改变洛威尔招生制度的决议中。

sentences.en: They said in language that Lowell's merit system had promoted white supremacy.
sentences.zh: 他们在决议中写道，洛威尔的精英选拔制度助长了白人至上主义。

sentences.en: Does it feel like they were, that kind of language conflates white people with Asian people?
sentences.zh: 这是否让你觉得，那种言论把白人和亚裔混为一谈了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Given that it's a majority Asian school.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这是一所以亚裔为主的学校。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: If I'm being honest, a lot of people I met, they actually forget that people of color includes Asians.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我遇到的很多人，他们实际上忘记了有色人种也包括亚裔。

sentences.en: They only think that people of color includes, uh, black and brown folks.
sentences.zh: 他们只认为有色人种包括，嗯，黑人和棕色人种。

sentences.en: And I think that many of these politicians also have that way of thought.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多政客也有这种思维方式。

sentences.en: They also think that people of color does not include Asians.
sentences.zh: 他们也认为有色人种不包括亚裔。

sentences.en: And I just wish that they would be more educated.
sentences.zh: 我只是希望他们能多受点教育。

sentences.en: This is one of the reasons we wanted to talk to Ben.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们想采访本的原因之一。

sentences.en: From all my time spent covering Asian American communities, I can tell you, this is the disconnect that comes up time and time again.
sentences.zh: 在我报道亚裔美国人社区的所有时间里，我可以告诉你，这就是一次又一次出现的认知脱节。

sentences.en: Alison Collins is not alone in characterizing Asians as white or white adjacent.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·柯林斯（Alison Collins）并不是唯一一个将亚裔描述为白人或“白人附庸”的人。

sentences.en: But for a lot of Asians, poor immigrant kids like Ben, whose parents don't speak any English and who have no idea how to steer him through a strange new country,
sentences.zh: 但对于许多亚裔来说，像本这样贫困的移民孩子，他们的父母不会说英语，也不知道如何引导他在一个陌生的新国家生活，

sentences.en: they don't really seem white at all.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来一点也不像白人。

sentences.en: Poor kids like Ben of any race don't typically have a lot of options or people looking out for them.
sentences.zh: 像本这样任何族裔的贫困孩子，通常都没有太多选择，也没有人照顾他们。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, these families have come to learn that Alison Collins and her family are wealthy and have resources that Ben and his friends don't.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这些家庭已经了解到，艾莉森·柯林斯和她的家人很富有，拥有的资源是本和他的朋友们所没有的。

sentences.en: And all this brings up another perennial question in this country.
sentences.zh: 而这一切引出了这个国家另一个永恒的问题。

sentences.en: When we talk about diversity, who are we talking about?
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论多元化时，我们到底在谈论谁？

sentences.en: Lowell is 82% non-white.
sentences.zh: 洛威尔高中82%的学生是非白人。

sentences.en: A third of its students come from families that are considered socioeconomically disadvantaged.
sentences.zh: 三分之一的学生来自被认为社会经济地位处于弱势的家庭。

sentences.en: Within the Chinese American students, that percentage is even higher.
sentences.zh: 在华裔美国学生中，这个比例甚至更高。

sentences.en: So how should we think about terms like diversity and equity?
sentences.zh: 那么我们应该如何看待“多元化”和“公平”这样的词汇？

sentences.en: What do those words mean when the interests of poor immigrant kids might be at odds with the interests of Black students,
sentences.zh: 当贫困移民孩子的利益可能与黑人学生的利益发生冲突时，这些词意味着什么？

sentences.en: who for years have been redlined out of the quote-unquote good schools, who do carry a burden of lowered expectations and suspicion?
sentences.zh: 他们多年来一直被所谓的“好学校”拒之门外，背负着被降低期望和被怀疑的负担。

sentences.en: So how do you resolve that conflict?
sentences.zh: 那么你该如何解决这种冲突呢？

sentences.en: There's a reason why this is one of the great debates playing out in America right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这是目前美国正在进行的重大辩论之一的原因。

sentences.en: But for a lot of Asians, they feel like they aren't even being included in that discussion.
sentences.zh: 但对于许多亚裔来说，他们觉得他们甚至没有被纳入那场讨论中。

sentences.en: I mean, why do you think people weren't listening to you?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你认为为什么人们不听你们的声音？

sentences.en: Asian Americans, we're the least representative groups in politics.
sentences.zh: 亚裔美国人，我们是政治上最缺乏代表性的群体。

sentences.en: So there's this culture also among Asian families to not get politically involved, right?
sentences.zh: 所以亚裔家庭中也存在一种不参与政治的文化，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, you know, we're immigrant families.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我们是移民家庭。

sentences.en: We came to this country.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这个国家。

sentences.en: And, you know, my parents, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我父母，对吧？

sentences.en: My parents, there's this viewpoint that we are in somebody else's country.
sentences.zh: 我父母，有一种观点认为我们是在别人的国家。

sentences.en: Therefore, we shouldn't have a huge say in it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不应该有太大的发言权。

sentences.en: And I believe that that's the perception among many Asian American families is to really be quiet on this issue, right?
sentences.zh: 我相信这就是许多亚裔美国人家庭的看法，即在这个问题上保持沉默，对吧？

sentences.en: And that is absolutely hurting Asian Americans in the process.
sentences.zh: 而这绝对是在伤害亚裔美国人。

sentences.en: Do you think that's changing?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种情况正在改变吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do feel that that's changing, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实觉得正在改变，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, for instance, my parents, they don't care about politics at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，例如，我父母，他们根本不关心政治。

sentences.en: But on this issue, they at least have some opinions about it, right?
sentences.zh: 但在这个问题上，他们至少有一些看法，对吧？

sentences.en: And they oppose this change.
sentences.zh: 而且他们反对这种改变。

sentences.en: And I do see that there is a future in which Asian Americans have a much larger say in how this country is run compared to now.
sentences.zh: 我确实看到未来亚裔美国人对这个国家的治理会有比现在大得多的发言权。

sentences.en: Do you know who I was recently talking to who surprised me with their recall vote?
sentences.zh: 你知道我最近和谁谈过，她的罢免投票让我感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Who?
sentences.zh: 谁？

sentences.en: My mom.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈。

sentences.en: At some point in reporting this story, I FaceTimed my mom just to check in.
sentences.zh: 在报道这个故事的某个阶段，我通过FaceTime和我妈通话，只是为了问候一下。

sentences.en: And I was telling her about what I was working on and that I might be coming out to San Francisco soon as part of my reporting.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她我正在做的工作，以及我可能很快会因为报道需要去旧金山。

sentences.en: And her response totally caught me off guard.
sentences.zh: 她的反应完全让我措手不及。

sentences.en: Did she vote no?
sentences.zh: 她投了反对票吗？

sentences.en: She voted yes.
sentences.zh: 她投了赞成票。

sentences.en: She recalled the school board, but she never votes.
sentences.zh: 她参与了罢免教委的投票，但她从不投票。

sentences.en: She's always thought that if you voted, you increase your likelihood of being drawn for jury selection.
sentences.zh: 她一直认为如果你投票，你被抽中担任陪审员的可能性就会增加。

sentences.en: So she just never voted.
sentences.zh: 所以她从来不投票。

sentences.en: And she's an American citizen?
sentences.zh: 她是美国公民吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, she's an American citizen.
sentences.zh: 是的，她是美国公民。

sentences.en: But she went out and voted for the recall?
sentences.zh: 但她还是出去投了罢免票？

sentences.en: Yeah, she did.
sentences.zh: 是的，她投了。

sentences.en: And I was like, I was on FaceTime with her, just catching up.
sentences.zh: 我当时正和她视频通话，只是在闲聊。

sentences.en: You should interview her.
sentences.zh: 你应该采访她。

sentences.en: I'm going to try.
sentences.zh: 我会试一试。

sentences.en: Seems like your parents are the ones that we should talk to.
sentences.zh: 看来你父母才是我们应该采访的对象。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm in my childhood bedroom with my mom.
sentences.zh: 我现在和我妈在我童年的卧室里。

sentences.en: And I'm going to ask her a few questions about my high school and about the recall race.
sentences.zh: 我要问她几个关于我高中和罢免选举的问题。

sentences.en: What's the recall race?
sentences.zh: 什么是罢免选举？

sentences.en: Recall race.
sentences.zh: 罢免选举。

sentences.en: Hey, let's help you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，让我们来帮你。

sentences.en: My family's story is a lot like Ben's family story.
sentences.zh: 我家的故事和本家的故事很像。

sentences.en: They immigrated here with no money and no diplomas.
sentences.zh: 他们移民到这里时没钱也没文凭。

sentences.en: My dad worked at a printing press, and my mom worked the grade for a shift at the airport.
sentences.zh: 我爸在印刷厂工作，我妈在机场做轮班工作。

sentences.en: Neither of them is fluent in English, and neither of them had heard of Lowell.
sentences.zh: 他们俩英语都不流利，也没听说过洛威尔高中。

sentences.en: And they were never political.
sentences.zh: 而且他们从不关心政治。

sentences.en: The idea of getting involved in anything outside of family or work was actually kind of scary to them.
sentences.zh: 参与家庭或工作以外的任何事情对他们来说其实都有点可怕。

sentences.en: Like, it would get them into trouble.
sentences.zh: 好像那会给他们惹麻烦一样。

sentences.en: And so, one of the things I was most curious about is how my mom even heard about the story.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最好奇的事情之一就是我妈是怎么听到这个消息的。

sentences.en: She says she heard about the admissions change at Lowell and the recall race last year.
sentences.zh: 她说她是去年听到关于洛威尔招生改革和罢免选举的消息的。

sentences.en: The Chinese language news channel, KTSF, had been reporting on parents who had been protesting over the Lowell emissions change.
sentences.zh: 中文新闻频道KTSF一直在报道那些抗议洛威尔招生改革的家长们。

sentences.en: She says this is how her Chinese friends and co-workers learned about it too, that if it hadn't been for KTSF, they wouldn't have known what was going on.
sentences.zh: 她说她的华裔朋友和同事也是这样得知的，如果不是因为KTSF，他们根本不会知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And what they heard made them feel it wasn't fair, that Asian students who had the merits to get in would be rejected by the more randomized system.
sentences.zh: 他们听到的内容让他们觉得这不公平，那些有能力考进去的亚裔学生会被这种更随机的制度拒之门外。

sentences.en: She also talked about learning through KTSF that the three board members who were up for recall had been more focused on renaming schools in the district
sentences.zh: 她还提到通过KTSF了解到，那三位面临罢免的教委成员在疫情期间，比起让孩子们重返校园，

sentences.en: than in getting kids back into school during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们更热衷于给学校改名。

sentences.en: Overall, my mom said, she felt like the board members weren't doing their jobs.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我妈说，她觉得这些教委成员没有尽到他们的职责。

sentences.en: But I asked her, but you've never been politically engaged before.
